To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the value of exercise stress testing, radionucleotide angiography and coronary artery angiography in predicting the occurrence of new coronary events in patients after a first uncomplicated episode of myocardial ischaemia was poor.

the exercise test, radionucleotide angiography and coronary arteriography are not helpful in the identification of the patient at high risk of a new coronary event two months after an acute uncomplicated myocardial event.

the exercise stress test, the radionuclide angiocardiography, and the coronary angiography are of no value for the prediction of a new coronary event in asymptomatic patients with previous myocardial infarct.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the prediction of coronary events in asymptotic patients after an uncomplicated myocardial event.
the value of the exercise electrocardiogram (ECG) and the radionuclide ventriculography in asymptomatic patients with previous myocardial infarctions.
the value of the exercise electrocardiogram, radionuclides and coronary angiography to predict new coronary events in patients with myocardial infarct who are symptom-free at the time of the study.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

, in the absence of symptoms, exercise testing and radionuclide studies do not predict new coronary events and that coronary angiography does not predict hard coronary events in asymptotic post-infarction patients.

, in asymptomatic patients who have suffered a first uncomplicated episode of myocardial, neither electrocardiographic stress testing nor radionuclide imaging or coronary angiography are useful for predicting new coronary events.
the value of exercise testing, radinuclide angiography and angiography is not high for the prediction of coronary events.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the risk of a new coronary event is high in the first year after a first uncomplicated myocardial event, but it is not possible to predict who will suffer such an event by means of non-invasive or invasive diagnostic tests.
the exercise test, radionucide angiography and angiography are not useful to predict new events in patients who have had an uncomplicated myocardial event.
in the absence of a positive test for ischemia, the risk of coronary events is very low.
The main takeaway from our work is that
exercise testing, radinuclide angiography, and coronary angiography do not help in identifying the risk of future coronary events in asymptotmic patients after a first myocardial infarct.
the exercise stress testing is not helpful two months post MI to predict future coronary events.
the exercise test and nuclear stress test are not helpful in predicting coronary events after an uncomplicated myocardial event.
